highlights.title: Tesla, Uber, and Waymo all get the OK to operate thousands of robotaxis in Nevada
highlights.description: Together, these permits would allow up to 8,000 robotaxis to be deployed over the next 12 months.

highlights.title: Can Anthropic Beat SpaceX’s Record IPO Size?
highlights.description: Anthropic expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX’s record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, in the latest sign of overwhelming demand from investors looking to profit from the artificial intelligence boom. Anthony Stephens has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Slack wants to drag AI coding out of the terminal and into the group chat
highlights.description: Slack wants to drag AI coding out of the terminal and into the group chat. The Salesforce-owned messaging platform today announced Slack Code, a new product that embeds AI coding agents — including Anthropic's Claude Code, Cognition's Devin, GitHub Copilot, and Vercel's agent — directly into dedicated Slack channels where entire teams can watch, steer, review, and ship software together. Slack Code is available on any Slack plan at launch, though customers need their own access to the partner ag

highlights.title: Musk Touts Starlink for India’s Rural Users Amid Stalled Launch
highlights.description: Billionaire Elon Musk pitched Starlink Inc.’s satellite-based internet service as a solution for India’s most underserved rural regions, even though the operator’s launch remains stalled in the country over security concerns.

highlights.title: Samsung Set to Top Phone Market in Downturn, Counterpoint Says
highlights.description: Samsung Electronics Co. will regain the top position in the smartphone market this year, in a sign of its greater resilience to higher memory-chip prices, Counterpoint Research predicted.

highlights.title: Humanoid Robots Put China Ahead in Tech Race
highlights.description: China’s humanoid robot makers now control 97% of global shipments, giving Beijing an early lead over U.S. rivals. At the World Robot Conference, robots sort boxes, handle laundry, and bag clothes, but the real test is whether they can become everyday tools. Bloomberg’s Allen Wan has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: The Single English County Saying No to Palantir
highlights.description: The UK government is facing calls to cancel a sprawling health care contract with Palantir. The region of Greater Manchester insists it can do a better job itself.

highlights.title: Tesla discontinues its Solar Roof tiles, not economically viable
highlights.description: Tesla has discontinued the Solar Roof, its solar-tile roofing product, Electrek has learned. The company has told third-party installers that it will no longer supply solar roof tiles going forward, only solar panels, according to two sources close to the program.

highlights.title: Fujifilm Expands Key Chip Material Output to Capture AI Demand
highlights.description: Fujifilm Holdings Corp. is expanding production of key materials used in advanced semiconductor manufacturing to capitalize on surging demand.

highlights.title: AI Spending Splurge Boosts Danfoss’s Bet on Data Center Cooling
highlights.description: Danfoss A/S expects its data-center business to at least double its share of the firm’s sales this year as the artificial-intelligence boom drives spending on the cooling equipment needed to run increasingly powerful chips.
